## Goal
- Produce evidence-based production end-to-end QA and audit verification without claiming unproven deployment or CI status.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Use only canonical repository `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform`.
- Do not create repositories, forks, duplicate projects, or temporary branches unless explicitly approved.
- Do not expose credentials, OTPs, passwords, bearer tokens, or personal test identities.
- Do not claim commit deployment, ownership, or full QA completion without verifiable evidence.
- Do not mutate production until deployed SHA and required QA gates are verified.

## Progress
### Done
- Re-probed public production surfaces successfully:
  ```text
  https://ivxholding.com → 200 text/html; charset=utf-8
  https://chat.ivxholding.com → 200 text/html; charset=utf-8
  https://api.ivxholding.com/health → 200 application/json
  https://api.ivxholding.com/version → 200
  https://api.ivxholding.com/readiness → 200
  ```
- Production `/health` reported:
  ```json
  {
    "ok": true,
    "status": "healthy",
    "aiStartupValidation": {
      "ok": true,
      "provider": "vercel_ai_gateway",
      "providerType": "vercel_gateway",
      "model": "openai/gpt-4o"
    },
    "seniorDeveloperRuntime": {
      "enabled": true,
      "commitSha": "012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c",
      "github": {"canReadRepo": true, "canPush": true},
      "render": {"canDeploy": true}
    },
    "ivxSeniorDeveloperFinalVerification": {
      "verified": true,
      "executionPath": "github_git_data_api",
      "commitSha": "012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c"
    }
  }
  ```
- Public-chat smoke request passed:
  ```text
  POST https://api.ivxholding.com/api/public/chat
  HTTP 200
  answer="The answer is 4."
  commit=012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c
  persistence=supabase
  ```
  - Response had `source:"fallback"`; it proves route availability and persistence, not primary AI-model execution.
- Member-verification CORS preflight passed:
  ```text
  OPTIONS /api/members/verification/send-code → 204
  ```
- Protected QA route correctly rejected unauthenticated access:
  ```text
  /api/ivx/autonomous/qa → 401
  ```
- Local static checks completed successfully:
  ```text
  bunx tsc --noEmit
  bunx tsc --noEmit && bun run lint   # expo; warnings only
  ```
- Android release consistency passes locally:
  ```text
  node scripts/verify-apk-release-consistency.mjs
  {"status":"ok","version":"1.9.4","landingReferences":4}
  ```
- Previously repaired four `expo/ivxholding-landing/index.html` APK/QR references to `v1.9.4`; parity with `expo/app.config.ts` and `expo/android/app/build.gradle` is now locally validated.
- Started complete local test commands:
  ```text
  bun test backend/
  bun test                 # cwd=expo
  ```
  - Output showed test execution; final complete pass/fail totals were not captured before output truncation.
- Confirmed autonomous-deploy rollback coverage exists:
  ```text
  backend/ivx-autonomous-coder.test.ts
  ```
  - Test asserts mismatched health-check commit triggers rollback and sets `productionVerified` to `false`.
- Confirmed plaintext fallback OTP persistence remains in `backend/services/ivx-member-verification.ts`.

### In Progress
- Capture definitive exit codes and totals for:
  ```text
  bun test backend/
  bun test                 # cwd=expo
  ```
- Determine whether the 55 claimed local commits are deployed; live runtime continues to identify only:
  ```text
  012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c
  ```
- Audit canonical GitHub Actions, commit graph, and deployment status after valid external canonical GitHub access is available.
- Determine whether public chat’s `source:"fallback"` is expected fallback behavior or primary-provider degradation.
- Complete authenticated member, owner, deployment, registration, login, verification, and error-path E2E using non-sensitive authorized test identities.

### Blocked
- Local GitHub credential remains invalid:
  ```text
  GET https://api.github.com/user → 401
  Bad credentials
  ```
- Canonical private repository/commit lookup without valid authentication returns:
  ```json
  {
    "message":"Not Found",
    "documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#get-a-commit",
    "status":"404"
  }
  ```
- Canonical GitHub Actions runs, deployment statuses, workflow logs, and commit graph cannot be independently verified from this environment.
- Render API lookup remains unverified:
  ```text
  GET https://api.render.com/v1/services/srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0 → HTTP 400
  ```
- Local checkout remote is not directly canonical GitHub:
  ```text
  origin=https://git:e2b-egress-managed@rork-git-router.rork-direct.workers.dev/git/j2l8t44588ix9ns7b57mu
  ```
- Local `main` is ahead of its configured router remote by three commits; production SHA `012bb088...` is absent from the local object database.
- Full Playwright, Android emulator, and iOS simulator execution has not been evidenced as green for deployed SHA `012bb088...`.
- Owner deployment and protected owner-flow E2E require an authenticated Supabase owner session:
  ```text
  IVX auth guard failed: invalid or expired Supabase session.
  ```

## Key Decisions
- Treat live `/health`, `/version`, `/readiness`, and public-chat responses as proof that SHA `012bb088...` is currently serving, not proof that all claimed local commits are deployed.
- Treat production self-reported GitHub/Render capability as runtime-health evidence only; retain external canonical API/CI verification as a separate required evidence domain.
- Do not certify complete production E2E or the 55 commits until canonical commit/deployment records and required CI results align with the live SHA.
- Treat public-chat `source:"fallback"` as an audit finding, not primary-AI verification.
- Keep the Android consistency repair local-only until a deployed canonical SHA is proven to contain it.
- Do not revert or commit the local generated blueprint timestamp automatically; it is an unrelated working-tree mutation produced during test activity.

## Next Steps
- 1. Re-run/capture full final results with explicit exit status:
  ```text
  bun test backend/
  bun test                 # cwd=expo
  ```
- 2. Obtain valid canonical GitHub authentication and verify:
  ```text
  GET https://api.github.com/user
  ```
- 3. Retrieve canonical `main` history, Actions runs, artifacts, deployment statuses, and deployed-SHA provenance for `012bb088...`.
- 4. Map the claimed 55 local commits, including `2b262204efb2f8c6cd7ed87a519b83cb83a52e93`, to canonical commits and Render deployments.
- 5. Verify correct Render API credential format and endpoint for `srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0`.
- 6. Run canonical Playwright, Android emulator, and iOS simulator workflows where supported.
- 7. Run authenticated registration, login, OTP verification, member, and owner flows with authorized non-sensitive test accounts.
- 8. Inspect production public-chat telemetry/configuration to explain fallback use without exposing secrets.
- 9. Replace plaintext `FallbackCodeRecord.code` storage with salted/hash-based verification and regression tests.
- 10. Resolve or discard the unrelated local blueprint timestamp mutation before any source-control action.
- 11. Issue certification only after deployed SHA, canonical commit history, CI artifacts, and end-to-end QA evidence agree.

## Critical Context
- Current live production identity:
  ```text

  commit=012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c
  commitShort=012bb088
  ```

- Latest checked local commit is:

- Earlier observed claimed local commit remains newer/different from production SHA:


  ```diff
  + "generatedAt": "2026-08-03T12:11:47.394Z"
  ```
- Expo lint has warnings, including unused symbols and import order/duplicate imports; it did not report fatal lint errors in the captured output.
- Existing OTP policy:
  ```text
  CODE_TTL_MINUTES = 10
  ```

2|name: auth
     3|description: Add user authentication with Google or Apple sign-in using Rork
     4|  Auth. Use when the user wants login, sign-in, sign-up, sessions, protected
     5|  routes, profiles, or user accounts.
     6|aliases:
     7|  - login
     8|  - sign up
     9|  - signup
    10|  - authentication
    11|  - session
    12|  - user account
    13|  - profile screen
    14|  - protected route
    15|---
    16|
    17|# Rork Auth
    18|
    19|Rork Auth provides OAuth authentication with Google and Apple sign-in for your app. The app talks directly to Rork's auth API — no backend needed.
    20|
    21|## Choosing an Auth System
    22|
    23|A project uses exactly ONE identity model — pick before writing any auth code:
    24|
    25|- **Google or Apple sign-in** → Rork Auth (this skill). Zero configuration.
    26|- **Email/password, magic links, phone OTP, or other providers** → Rork Auth does NOT support these. Use **native Supabase Auth** instead — read the backend skill's `supabase/native-auth.md` and skip this skill entirely.
    27|
    28|
    29|**Never mix the two models.** Do not bolt `supabase.auth.signUp` / `signInWithPassword` onto an app that uses Rork Auth, and never create a second Supabase client to bypass the `accessToken` restriction — the error `supabase.auth.signUp is not possible` means the project is in Rork Auth mode, not that you should work around the client. Mixing produces two incompatible user-ID systems in the same tables and silently breaks RLS.
    30|
    31|If the user asks for email/password on a project that already uses Rork Auth, tell them the trade-off (existing sign-ins won't carry over) and, if they confirm, switch the whole app: call the backend skill's `disableRorkAuth`, rewrite RLS from `user_id()` to `auth.uid()`, and replace the auth flow with `native-auth.md`'s.
    32|
    33|## Auth Flow (all platforms)
    34|
    35|1. User taps "Sign in with Google/Apple"
    36|2. App opens an in-app browser (or `ASWebAuthenticationSession` on Swift) for OAuth
    37|3. After login, the browser redirects back to the app with an authorization code
    38|4. App exchanges the code for tokens directly with Rork
    39|5. App stores tokens securely and the user is logged in
    40|
    41|
    42|Access tokens are short-lived JWTs (1 hour). Refresh tokens are used to get new access tokens.
    43|
    44|## Setup Checklist (all platforms)
    45|
    46|1. [ ] Call the `getOrCreateAuthConfig` tool to provision auth keys and set environment variables
    47|2. [ ] Install the platform's auth/secure-storage dependencies
    48|3. [ ] Register the deep-link callback (URL scheme / entitlement)
    49|4. [ ] Create the auth state holder (`AuthProvider` + `useAuth` on RN; `AuthManager` on Swift)
    50|5. [ ] Wire the auth holder into the app's root
    51|6. [ ] Add the sign-in UI
    52|
    53|
    54|## Provisioning
    55|
    56|Call the `getOrCreateAuthConfig` tool. It provisions the app's public key and auth URL, and sets these environment variables. If the project has a Supabase backend, it also registers Rork Auth on it (so `user_id()` works in RLS) — watch the tool output: if it reports the backend already uses native Supabase Auth, stop and resolve the model conflict with the user instead of wiring Rork JWTs into Supabase.
    57|
    58|| Variable                    | Purpose                                         |
    59|| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
    60|| `EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_APP_KEY`  | Public client app key — safe to embed in client |
    61|| `EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_AUTH_URL` | Base URL for Rork's auth API                    |
    62|| `EXPO_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID`    | Project ID — used to derive the callback scheme |
    63|
    64|The callback URL scheme on every platform is `rork-<EXPO_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID>://auth/callback`.
    65|
    66|## Endpoints
    67|
    68|| Method | Path              | Purpose                                                 |
    69|| ------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
    70|| POST   | `/oauth/initiate` | Get the OAuth authorization URL for the chosen provider |
    71|| POST   | `/oauth/token`    | Exchange the returned authorization code for tokens     |
    72|| POST   | `/oauth/refresh`  | Refresh an expired access token                         |
    73|
    74|All three accept JSON. `/oauth/initiate` takes `{ app_key, provider, code_challenge, target, env, app_path? }` and returns `{ auth_url, state }`. `/oauth/token` takes `{ app_key, code, code_verifier }` and returns `{ access_token, refresh_token, user }`. `/oauth/refresh` takes `{ app_key, refresh_token }` and returns `{ access_token, expires_in }`.
    75|
    76|`provider` is either `"google"` or `"apple"`. `target` is `"rn"` for React Native, `"swift"` for Swift, or `"web"` for Vite + React web apps. `env` is `"native"` on device, `"preview"` for both the React Native web preview and the Vite web preview (inside the Rork iframe), `"simulator"` on the iOS Simulator, or `"production"` for a deployed Vite web app. `app_path` is optional and only used when `env === "preview"` — it selects the preview subdomain (e.g. `"web"` for Vite, `"expo"` for RN, which is the default fallback).
    77|
    78|## Authenticated API Requests
    79|
    80|Send the stored access token as a bearer token to your app's backend:
    81|
    82|```
    83|Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
    84|
    85|```
    86|
    87|## Platform Implementation Guides
    88|
    89|The implementation differs per platform — read the file matching the app you're working in:
    90|
    91|| File              | When to use                                                                      |
    92|| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    93|| `react-native.md` | React Native / Expo apps (uses `expo-web-browser` + `expo-secure-store`)         |
    94|| `swift.md`        | Swift / iOS apps (uses `ASWebAuthenticationSession` + Keychain)                  |
    95|| `web.md`          | Vite + React web apps (uses `window.open` / top-level redirect + `localStorage`) |
    96|
    97|## Important Notes
    98|
    99|- The app talks directly to Rork's auth API — no backend auth routes needed.
   100|- Always use HTTPS in production.
   101|- Keychain / SecureStore data persists across app reinstalls; call `signOut()` if needed during development.
   102|
   103|
   104|## Available tools
   105|
   106|### getOrCreateAuthConfig
   107|
   108|Create or retrieve the auth configuration (public app key and auth URL) for this app. Use this when setting up Rork Auth for the first time. The returned values are automatically stored as environment variables.
   109|
   110|```json
   111|{"type":"object","properties":{}}
   112|```

(End of file - total 112 lines)

2|name: backend
     3|description: Add server-side capabilities to a Rork project — including
     4|  Supabase, Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, realtime/multiplayer, webhooks,
     5|  scheduled tasks, and edge functions. Routes between Cloudflare-first and
     6|  Supabase-first internally.
     7|aliases:
     8|  - server
     9|  - api
    10|  - webhook
    11|  - realtime
    12|  - multiplayer
    13|  - database
    14|  - persistence
    15|  - durable object
    16|  - worker
    17|  - supabase
    18|---
    19|
    20|# Backend
    21|
    22|Use this skill for backend work in Rork projects. There are two modern services and one legacy stack:
    23|
    24|- **Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects** — portable server-side code, realtime connection handling, and scoped durable SQLite storage. This is the default for APIs, webhooks, business logic, validation, third-party integrations, scheduled tasks, realtime, multiplayer, and per-room/per-project state. Read .rork/skills/backend/cloudflare/overview.md.
    25|- **Supabase Postgres** — managed relational SQL storage with Row Level Security. Use it when the app needs global relational queries, RLS-protected client access, reporting, or data that should not be partitioned by Durable Object identity. Read .rork/skills/backend/supabase/overview.md.
    26|- **Legacy Hono + tRPC** — only for projects that already have `backend/hono.ts`. Read .rork/skills/backend/legacy-hono/overview.md.
    27|
    28|
    29|## Default to Cloudflare for Code
    30|
    31|If you are adding any server-side code, prefer Cloudflare Workers. The Worker is vanilla Cloudflare (`export default { fetch }`) and can be lifted into a normal Cloudflare account with a `wrangler.jsonc` if the project ever needs to migrate off Rork. That portability also makes future bug fixes and backwards-compatible API evolution easier: the code owns the API boundary instead of spreading behavior across client calls and database policies.
    32|
    33|Use Cloudflare for:
    34|
    35|- API endpoints called by React Native, Swift, or web apps.
    36|- Webhook handlers (Stripe, Resend, GitHub, etc.).
    37|- Business logic, validation, permissions beyond simple row ownership, third-party API calls, and response shaping.
    38|- Realtime, multiplayer, chat, presence, collaborative state, WebSockets, and scheduled tasks via Durable Objects.
    39|- Durable Object storage when the data naturally belongs to one room, one match, one user session, one document, or one project-scoped actor.
    40|
    41|
    42|## Choose the Data Layer
    43|
    44|Cloudflare can be the database too. Durable Objects include per-object SQLite storage (`this.ctx.storage.sql`), so a Worker can own both the API and the durable state without adding Supabase.
    45|
    46|Use **Durable Object storage** when:
    47|
    48|- The app needs multiplayer rooms, presence, chat, matchmaking, collaborative documents, or any WebSocket fanout.
    49|- State is naturally scoped to a stable id such as `roomId`, `matchId`, `documentId`, `userId`, or `projectId`.
    50|- You want one colocated authority for connections plus data: the DO handles sockets, writes SQLite rows, runs periodic timers, and serves reads.
    51|- The data is small to medium, local to that object, and does not need global SQL joins across every project/user.
    52|
    53|
    54|Use **Supabase Postgres** when:
    55|
    56|- The app needs global relational queries, cross-user reporting, search/filtering across many records, SQL joins, or admin analytics.
    57|- The client should read/write directly with Row Level Security.
    58|- The data should live in one central relational database instead of being partitioned across Durable Object instances.
    59|
    60|
    61|Common patterns:
    62|
    63|1. **Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object storage** (default for realtime and scoped state). The Worker/DO owns both API and data.
    64|2. **Cloudflare Worker -> Supabase** (recommended for non-trivial logic over relational data). The Worker owns the public API and calls Supabase as the database.
    65|3. **Client -> Supabase directly with RLS** (acceptable for thin CRUD like TODOs, profile editing, simple user-owned records). RLS guards rows, and there is little or no custom server-side behavior.
    66|
    67|
    68|Move from direct client access to a Worker-owned API as soon as business logic grows. RLS is useful, but it is Supabase-specific; portable behavior belongs in Cloudflare code when possible.
    69|
    70|## Edge Function Choice
    71|
    72|Prefer Cloudflare Workers over Supabase Edge Functions. Use Supabase Edge Functions only when the function must run inside Supabase's environment with elevated database privileges or Supabase-specific auth context. For normal APIs and integrations, use Cloudflare.
    73|
    74|## Existing Projects
    75|
    76|Never migrate an existing Supabase-based project to Cloudflare just because Cloudflare is the default for new code. Continue the existing architecture unless the user explicitly asks for migration. The portability principle is for choosing where to put new behavior, not for creating churn.
    77|
    78|For legacy `backend/hono.ts` projects, extend the existing stack unless the user explicitly asks to migrate.

(End of file - total 78 lines)

## FINAL QA verdict: **BLOCKED**

**Production evidence captured**
- Repository: `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform`
- Live backend: `https://api.ivxholding.com`
- Live web: `https://ivxholding.com`
- Health/version/web: **HTTP 200**
- Live backend SHA: `012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c`
- Anonymous owner-only QA route: **401** (expected access control)
- Invalid registration: **400 / VALIDATING**, no account creation.

**Local security repairs staged, not deployed**
- `backend/services/ivx-member-verification.ts`
  - OTP persistence changed from plaintext to salted `scrypt` hashes.
  - Constant-time verification, expiry, single-use state, failed-attempt limit, resend limit.
  - OTP is no longer returned by the service response.
- `backend/api/ivx-members.ts`
  - Gender is optional when omitted.
  - Password-confirmation mismatch is rejected.

**Validation**
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — **PASS**
- `bun test backend/ivx-registration-orchestrator.test.ts backend/ivx-autonomous-coder.test.ts` — **38 pass, 0 fail**
- No production deployment, commit, or mobile build was performed.

**Why final certification cannot pass**
1. Canonical GitHub API access is unavailable (private repo returns 404 / credentials earlier returned 401); no canonical HEAD, CI URL, merge, or Actions result can be proven.
2. The live SHA predates the local OTP repair, so production OTP storage remains unverified/insecure.
3. No approved authenticated owner session or non-sensitive test-member flow is available; member creation, OTP delivery, Supabase record verification, sign-in/reset, and owner module access were not executed.
4. Android/iOS/web platform E2E has not been executed against one SHA-matched production release.
5. Render deployment ID and GitHub–Render SHA parity cannot be independently verified.

I will not claim member registration, owner sign-in, database synchronization, or OTP security as production-passed until the canonical branch can be authenticated, the repairs are reviewed/deployed, and the authenticated QA matrix is run.
